The maximum payload length in a UDP frame is 1444 bytes (without fragmentation).
We use 4 bytes to hold the sequence number so 1440 bytes are avaialble for data.
When the code detects that the frame is for the specified port then the MSB
of the sequence number is received.  We then read the next 3 bytes to complete the
sequence number.  Hence at the end of the sequence number the byte_number is 2.
We then accumulate 4 bytes to form a 32 bit value i.e. 16 bit + 16 bit sample.
At the end of the accumulation the byte_number will be 6 in which case we need to save the sample
in the FIFO by setting fifo_wrreq true.  Only write to the fifo if not full.

JB: some conclusions of sprite engine investigation, it seems to be as follows:
- during vblank sprite dma is disabled by hardware, no automatic fetches occur but copper or cpu
can write to any sprite register, and all SPRxPTR pointers should be refreshed
- during the last line of vblank (PAL: $19, NTSC: $14) if sprite dma is enabled
it fetches SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL registers according to current SPRxPTR pointers
This is the only chance for DMA to fetch new values of SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL. If DMA isn't enabled
during this line new values won't be placed into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL registers.
Enabling DMA after this line can have two results depending on current value of SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL.
- if VSTOP value is matched first with VERBEAM, data from memory is fetched and placed into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL
- or if VSTART value is matched with VERBEAM, data from memory is fetched and placed into SPRxDATA/SPRxDATB
and the situation repeats with every new line until VSTOP condition is met.
If you set VSTART to value lower or the same (remember that VSTOP takes precedence) as the current VERBEAM
this condition will never be met and sprite engine will wait till VSTOP matches VERBEAM. If it happens then it
fetches another two words into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL. And again if new VSTART is lower or the same as VERBEAM
it will fetch another new SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL when VSTOP is met (or will wait till next vbl).
To disable further sprite list processing it's enough to set VSTART and VSTOP to values which are outside
of the screen or has been already achieved.
When waiting for VSTART condition any write to SPRxDATA (write to SPRxDATB takes no effect) makes the written value
visible on the screen but it doesn't start DMA although it's enabled. The same value is displayed in every subsequent
line until DMA starts and delivers new data to SPRxDAT or SPRxCTL is written (by DMA, copper or cpu).
It seems like only VSTART condition starts DMA transfer.
Any write to SPRxCTL while DMA is active doesn't stop display but new value of VSTOP takes effect. Actually
display is reenabled by DMA write to SPRxDATA in next line.
The same applies to SPRxPOS writes when sprite is beeing displayed - only HSTART position changes (if new VSTART
is specified to be met before VSTOP nothing interesting happens).
The DMA engine sees VSTART condition as true even if DMA is dissabled. Enabling DMA after VSTART and before VSTOP
starts sprite display in enabled line (if it's enabled early enough).
Dissabling DMA in the line when new SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL is fetched and enabling it in the next one results in stopped
DMA transfer but the last line of sprite is displayed till the end of the screen.
VSTART and VSTOP specified within vbl are not met.
The first possible line to display a sprite is line $1A (PAL).
During vbl SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL are not automatically modified, values written before vbl are still present when vbl ends.
if vbl or VSTOP : disable data dma
else if VSTART: start data dma
if vblend or (VSTOP and not vbl): dma transfer to sprxpos/sprxctl
else if data dma active: transfer to sprxdata/sprcdatb
It doesn't seem to be complicated :)
Sprite which has been triggered by write to SPRxDATA is not disabled by vbl.
It seems that vstop and vstart conditions are checked every cycle.
Dma doesn't fetch new pos/ctl if vstop is not equal to the current line number.
If new vstart is specified to be the same as the line during which it's fetched, display starts in the next line

JB: some conclusions of sprite engine investigation, it seems to be as follows:
- during vblank sprite dma is disabled by hardware, no automatic fetches occur but copper or cpu
can write to any sprite register, and all SPRxPTR pointers should be refreshed
- during the last line of vblank (PAL: $19, NTSC: $14) if sprite dma is enabled
it fetches SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL registers according to current SPRxPTR pointers
This is the only chance for DMA to fetch new values of SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL. If DMA isn't enabled
during this line new values won't be placed into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL registers.
Enabling DMA after this line can have two results depending on current value of SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL.
- if VSTOP value is matched first with VERBEAM, data from memory is fetched and placed into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL
- or if VSTART value is matched with VERBEAM, data from memory is fetched and placed into SPRxDATA/SPRxDATB
and the situation repeats with every new line until VSTOP condition is met.
If you set VSTART to value lower or the same (remember that VSTOP takes precedence) as the current VERBEAM
this condition will never be met and sprite engine will wait till VSTOP matches VERBEAM. If it happens then it
fetches another two words into SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL. And again if new VSTART is lower or the same as VERBEAM
it will fetch another new SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL when VSTOP is met (or will wait till next vbl).
To disable further sprite list processing it's enough to set VSTART and VSTOP to values which are outside
of the screen or has been already achieved.
When waiting for VSTART condition any write to SPRxDATA (write to SPRxDATB takes no effect) makes the written value
visible on the screen but it doesn't start DMA although it's enabled. The same value is displayed in every subsequent
line until DMA starts and delivers new data to SPRxDAT or SPRxCTL is written (by DMA, copper or cpu).
It seems like only VSTART condition starts DMA transfer.
Any write to SPRxCTL while DMA is active doesn't stop display but new value of VSTOP takes effect. Actually
display is reenabled by DMA write to SPRxDATA in next line.
The same applies to SPRxPOS writes when sprite is beeing displayed - only HSTART position changes (if new VSTART
is specified to be met before VSTOP nothing interesting happens).
The DMA engine sees VSTART condition as true even if DMA is dissabled. Enabling DMA after VSTART and before VSTOP
starts sprite display in enabled line (if it's enabled early enough).
Dissabling DMA in the line when new SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL is fetched and enabling it in the next one results in stopped
DMA transfer but the last line of sprite is displayed till the end of the screen.
VSTART and VSTOP specified within vbl are not met.
The first possible line to display a sprite is line $1A (PAL).
During vbl SPRxPOS/SPRxCTL are not automatically modified, values written before vbl are still present when vbl ends.
if vbl or VSTOP : disable data dma
else if VSTART: start data dma
if vblend or (VSTOP and not vbl): dma transfer to sprxpos/sprxctl
else if data dma active: transfer to sprxdata/sprcdatb
It doesn't seem to be complicated :)
Sprite which has been triggered by write to SPRxDATA is not disabled by vbl.
It seems that vstop and vstart conditions are checked every cycle.
Dma doesn't fetch new pos/ctl if vstop is not equal to the current line number.
If new vstart is specified to be the same as the line during which it's fetched, display starts in the next line

.serdes_tx_forcedisp(2'b00),			//if we force disparity, it's always to negative
//Wait for MAC reset to come in
//Wait 2^15 cycles (~525 us) to reset after powerup so everything initializes OK.
//Don't start the timer until the transceiver PLL has locked so we have stable clocks to work with!
//We want to have commas LEFT aligned, but the SERDES tries to *right* align them!
//Fix that by adding 2 cycles of latency.
//Byte-swap 16-bit words since it looks like base-X sends config words in a strange endianness
//Reset disparity to negative when link comes up
//Config register as of when we entered the current state
//Transmit pipeline registers (need to add a cycle of latency for inserting the CRC)
//If sending /C1/ during configuration, force disparity negative
//If in autonegotiation mode, send the status register
//If we have data to read, but didn't already start the read process, pop the next word
//We haven't kicked off the send yet.
//Send a SPD (K27.7) followed by a 0x55 to align the packet to a 16-bit boundary
//Data to read? get the next word
//If no more data to read, go into the end sequence
//These codes do not change the disparity
//Send idles if nothing else to send
//Go on if we get a good config register (supports full duplex)
//Set our ACK bit and wait for the other end to do the same
//If we get good results, move on
//If the timer elapses and we have stable state, we're good to go
//Wait for the remote end to start sending igle bits
//If we get idles, good to go
//Restart the link timer every time we get a valid triple of idle words
//If the timer wraps, the link has gone down
//(this means that we have to get at least 3 idles in a row every 10 ms to stay up)
//If we get a configuration word the link has gone down so restart autonegotiation
//3 = next data word goes at [7:0] and [31:23] of next
//Reset CRC when a new frame begins
//Feed data in if we're looking at data
//0 deg: checksum the entire incoming message
//90 deg: checksum the saved byte and half of the incoming message
//180 deg: checksum the entire incoming message
//270 deg:checksum the saved byte and half of the incoming message
//Even/odd packet lengths need different phase offsets
//Delay old CRCs by a cycle so we can read the value we are comparing against
//Indicates we saw a valid frame or idle code this cycle
//Assert data-ready if we have any data ready to send
//Zero out the CRC so we have a nice clean data field
//Even/odd packet lengths need different phase offsets
//SFD in first byte, second is data
//0 deg offset... load into left half
//180 deg offset... load into right half and then send it
//270 deg offset... load into right quarter, send it, then load into left quarter

The maximum payload length in a UDP frame is 1444 bytes (without fragmentation).
We use 4 bytes to hold the sequence number so 1440 bytes are avaialble for data.
When the code detects that the frame is for the specified port then the MSB
of the sequence number is received.  We then read the next 3 bytes to complete the
sequence number.  Hence at the end of the sequence number the byte_number is 2.
We then accumulate 4 bytes to form a 32 bit value i.e. 16 bit + 16 bit sample.
At the end of the accumulation the byte_number will be 6 in which case we need to save the sample
in the FIFO by setting fifo_wrreq true.  Only write to the fifo if not full.

Pulse Width Generators/timers with 16-bit main counter.
Period or timers target number is controlled by register [15:0]period.
Duty cycle is controlled by register [15:0]DC.
Clock used for PWM signal generation can be switched between Wishbone Bus clock and external clock. It is down clocked first.
o_pwm outputs PWM signal or timers interrupt.
bit 0:	When set, external clock is chosen for PWM/timer. When cleared, wb clock is used for PWM/timer.
bit 1:	When set,  PWM is enabled. When cleared,  timer is enabled.
bit 2:	When set,  PWM/timer starts. When cleared, PWM/timer stops.
bit 3:	When set, timer runs continuously. When cleared, timer runs one time.
bit 5:	timer interrupt bit	When it is written with 0, interrupt request is cleared.
bit 6:	When set, a 16-bit external signal i_DC is used as duty cycle. When cleared, register DC is used.
bit 7:	When set, counter reset for PWM/timer, it's output and bit 5 will also be cleared. When changing from PWM mode to timer mode reset is needed before timer starts.

//Wait for MAC reset to come in
//Wait 2^15 cycles (~525 us) to reset after powerup so everything initializes OK.
//Don't start the timer until the transceiver PLL has locked so we have stable clocks to work with!
//We want to have commas LEFT aligned, but the SERDES tries to *right* align them!
//Fix that by adding 2 cycles of latency.
//Byte-swap 16-bit words since it looks like base-X sends config words in a strange endianness
//Reset disparity to negative when link comes up
//Config register as of when we entered the current state
//Transmit pipeline registers (need to add a cycle of latency for inserting the CRC)
//If sending /C1/ during configuration, force disparity negative
//If in autonegotiation mode, send the status register
//If we have data to read, but didn't already start the read process, pop the next word
//We haven't kicked off the send yet.
//Send a SPD (K27.7) followed by a 0x55 to align the packet to a 16-bit boundary
//Data to read? get the next word
//If no more data to read, go into the end sequence
//These codes do not change the disparity
//Send idles if nothing else to send
//Go on if we get a good config register (supports full duplex)
//Set our ACK bit and wait for the other end to do the same
//If we get good results, move on
//If the timer elapses and we have stable state, we're good to go
//Wait for the remote end to start sending igle bits
//If we get idles, good to go
//Restart the link timer every time we get a valid triple of idle words
//If the timer wraps, the link has gone down
//(this means that we have to get at least 3 idles in a row every 10 ms to stay up)
//If we get a configuration word the link has gone down so restart autonegotiation
//3 = next data word goes at [7:0] and [31:23] of next
//Reset CRC when a new frame begins
//Feed data in if we're looking at data
//0 deg: checksum the entire incoming message
//90 deg: checksum the saved byte and half of the incoming message
//180 deg: checksum the entire incoming message
//270 deg:checksum the saved byte and half of the incoming message
//Even/odd packet lengths need different phase offsets
//Delay old CRCs by a cycle so we can read the value we are comparing against
//Indicates we saw a valid frame or idle code this cycle
//Assert data-ready if we have any data ready to send
//Zero out the CRC so we have a nice clean data field
//Even/odd packet lengths need different phase offsets
//SFD in first byte, second is data
//0 deg offset... load into left half
//180 deg offset... load into right half and then send it
//270 deg offset... load into right quarter, send it, then load into left quarter

Pulse Width Generators/timers with 16-bit main counter.
Period or timers target number is controlled by register [15:0]period.
Duty cycle is controlled by register [15:0]DC.
Clock used for PWM signal generation can be switched between Wishbone Bus clock and external clock. It is down clocked first.
o_pwm outputs PWM signal or timers interrupt.
bit 0:	When set, external clock is chosen for PWM/timer. When cleared, wb clock is used for PWM/timer.
bit 1:	When set,  PWM is enabled. When cleared,  timer is enabled.
bit 2:	When set,  PWM/timer starts. When cleared, PWM/timer stops.
bit 3:	When set, timer runs continuously. When cleared, timer runs one time.
bit 5:	timer interrupt bit	When it is written with 0, interrupt request is cleared.
bit 6:	When set, a 16-bit external signal i_DC is used as duty cycle. When cleared, register DC is used.
bit 7:	When set, counter reset for PWM/timer, it's output and bit 5 will also be cleared. When changing from PWM mode to timer mode reset is needed before timer starts.
